description: Make Ralph very easy to start, invoke, inspect, and recover with non-destructive diagnostics, optional global invocation, clearer onboarding, a worked example, and a self-guided flowchart.

userStories.title: Add CLI doctor mode
userStories.description: As a first-time Ralph user, I want a preflight command so that I can verify my environment and state before starting a run.
acceptanceCriteria: ./ralph.sh --doctor checks required binaries, prompt files, repo-local skills, and Ralph state files
Doctor output labels each check as pass or fail and includes one concrete next action for each failure
Doctor exits with status 0 only when all required checks pass
Doctor is non-destructive and does not mutate Ralph state
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Add CLI status mode
userStories.description: As an active Ralph user, I want a status command so that I can see progress and the next pending story without reading raw JSON.
acceptanceCriteria: ./ralph.sh --status reports current branchName, total story count, passed story count, pending story count, and the next pending story ID and title
Status output includes the exact paths to prd.json, progress.txt, and archive/
If prd.json is missing or invalid, status explains the exact next command or file the user should use
Status is non-destructive and does not start an iteration
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Tighten CLI error recovery guidance
userStories.description: As a new Ralph user, I want every common failure to tell me the next step so that I do not need to inspect source code to recover.
acceptanceCriteria: Invalid flags explicitly point to ./ralph.sh --help
Missing tool binaries explain which binary is missing and which command path the user should take next
Missing or invalid prd.json explains the Codex-first sequence $prd -> $ralph -> ./ralph.sh
Errors caused by missing prompt or skill files explain which repo files must exist and where they should live
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Add a global Ralph command
userStories.description: As a developer using Ralph across projects, I want a simple one-time install path so that I can run ralph without remembering the repo-local ./ralph.sh path every time.
acceptanceCriteria: The repo provides a documented install path that exposes ralph on PATH after one-time setup
The installed ralph command runs the same loop as ./ralph.sh with Codex as the default runtime
The global command supports the same flags as ./ralph.sh, or any intentional differences are explicitly documented
Documentation explains when to use ralph versus ./ralph.sh and how to undo the install
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Add a copy-paste quickstart
userStories.description: As a developer trying Ralph for the first time, I want a short copy-paste quickstart so that I can reach a first run with minimal interpretation.
acceptanceCriteria: README.md contains a short quickstart section with the smallest successful Codex-first flow
The quickstart includes $prd, $ralph, ./ralph.sh, and at least one progress inspection command that does not require jq knowledge
The quickstart links to or references --help, --doctor, and --status
Claude guidance remains present but clearly secondary to the Codex path
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Ship a worked example
userStories.description: As a new Ralph user, I want one realistic example I can copy so that I can follow a known-good workflow instead of inventing my own.
acceptanceCriteria: The repo includes one small worked example that starts with a feature idea and ends with a valid prd.json
The example uses current repo conventions and file paths
The example is small enough that its stories are credible one-iteration Ralph tasks
The example is referenced from README.md
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Add troubleshooting and recovery docs
userStories.description: As a Ralph user, I want explicit recovery instructions so that I can resume, restart, or debug a broken run without guessing.
acceptanceCriteria: Documentation explains how to handle missing prd.json, invalid prd.json, empty progress.txt, branch changes, and archived runs
Documentation distinguishes continuing the current run from starting a new run
Each recovery path includes exact commands or file locations, not just conceptual guidance
Recovery guidance is reachable from the main README
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Align the flowchart with the real workflow
userStories.description: As a user learning Ralph visually, I want the flowchart content to match the repo so that the diagram reinforces the actual process.
acceptanceCriteria: The flowchart uses the current Codex-first sequence $prd -> $ralph -> ./ralph.sh
The flowchart names the real state files prd.json, progress.txt, and archive/
The flowchart reflects the one-story-per-iteration behavior described in CODEX.md
cd flowchart && npm run build passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Make the flowchart self-guided
userStories.description: As a first-time visitor, I want the flowchart to explain where to start and what to click next so that I can learn Ralph without a presenter.
acceptanceCriteria: The flowchart has a clear entry state for first-time viewers
The flowchart gives visible progression cues as steps are revealed
The main interaction remains usable on desktop and mobile widths
cd flowchart && npm run build passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
Typecheck passes
